description: Front-line commercial rep responsible for face-to-face engagement with healthcare professionals (HCPs). Carries a territory, manages account plans, executes calls/visits, delivers approved content, and collects sample signatures.
key_workflows: Pre-call planning — review account history, last interactions, and open objectives before each visit
Visit execution — check in at location, present CLM content, capture discussion notes, collect signatures for samples
Sample management — record sample drops, verify lot numbers, check allocation limits, capture HCP signatures on a mobile device
Activity reporting — log call reports, record next-step commitments, sync data from the field
Territory management — view alignment, manage routing, track visit frequency compliance
common_challenges: Offline access — reps need full functionality in hospitals/clinics with no connectivity
Signature capture — must work reliably on tablet with legal compliance (21 CFR Part 11 in regulated markets)
Data sync conflicts — edits made offline may conflict with changes pushed by operations
Content relevance — reps need the right content for each HCP specialty, not a generic library
Compliance visibility — must see real-time sample limits and call frequency caps

description: Strategic account owner managing large institutional accounts (hospitals, IDNs, health systems). Focuses on account-level planning, multi-stakeholder engagement, and long-term contracting rather than individual rep-level calls.
key_workflows: Account planning — build engagement plans spanning multiple stakeholders within an institution
Stakeholder mapping — identify decision makers, influencers, and budget holders across departments
Meeting orchestration — coordinate cross-functional visits involving medical, commercial, and market access teams
Contract management — track formulary status, pricing agreements, and procurement timelines
Performance dashboards — monitor account-level KPIs (revenue, market share, adherence, formulary wins)
common_challenges: Complex org hierarchies — accounts span multiple sites, subsidiaries, and affiliates with shared decision-making
Multi-team coordination — KAM must align field reps, MSLs, and market access across the same account
Long sales cycles — institutional decisions take months; tracking engagement across quarters is essential
Data aggregation — need a unified view across all contacts, interactions, and contracts at the account level
Regulatory constraints — different engagement rules for procurement vs. clinical stakeholders

description: Non-promotional scientific expert who engages key opinion leaders (KOLs) with medical and scientific information. Operates under strict compliance boundaries separating medical and commercial interactions.
key_workflows: KOL engagement — maintain scientific relationships with thought leaders, track publication co-authorships, congress attendance
Medical inquiry response — handle unsolicited medical information requests, log responses and approved references
Congress and event management — plan booth engagement, poster sessions, and 1:1 meetings at medical congresses
Publication tracking — monitor KOL publication activity and relevant clinical trial data
Insight capture — record field medical insights to feed product development and medical strategy
common_challenges: Compliance firewall — strict separation between commercial and medical activities; MSLs must not engage in promotional discussions
Interaction documentation — every KOL touchpoint must be documented with compliant classification (scientific exchange vs. promotional)
Content limitations — MSLs can only share approved scientific content, not marketing materials
Cross-functional visibility — MSLs need to see commercial activity without participating in it, to avoid duplication
Publication and congress data — need integration with external publication databases and congress schedules

description: Operations leader responsible for territory alignment, data quality, field force effectiveness, and reporting. Configures and maintains the CRM for the commercial team.
key_workflows: Territory alignment — design and maintain territory hierarchies, assign reps to geographies and accounts
Data stewardship — manage HCP/HCO master data, handle duplicates, maintain data quality metrics
Field force configuration — set up call plans, cycle frequencies, activity plan templates, and business rules
Reporting and analytics — build dashboards for call compliance, reach/frequency, sample utilization, and territory coverage
User administration — manage profiles, permission sets, feature flags, and role hierarchies
common_challenges: Alignment changes — territory realignments happen 1-2x per year and require careful data migration
Downstream dependencies — changes to territories cascade to call plans, sample allocations, and reporting hierarchies
Data quality — HCP/HCO data degrades rapidly; need automated deduplication and enrichment
Cross-module configuration — a single business rule change (e.g., call frequency cap) may span multiple modules
Reporting latency — leadership expects real-time dashboards but data sync from mobile introduces lag

description: Regulatory compliance leader ensuring all field activities adhere to industry regulations (PDMA, Sunshine Act, GDPR, local pharma codes). Reviews and approves content, monitors sample inventory, and manages consent.
key_workflows: Sample audit — review sample distribution reports, verify chain-of-custody, reconcile inventory against regulatory limits
Consent management — configure and monitor opt-in/opt-out status for all communication channels per jurisdiction
Content approval — review and approve marketing materials, emails, and CLM presentations before field deployment
Transparency reporting — generate aggregate spend reports for Sunshine Act / EFPIA disclosure requirements
Adverse event monitoring — ensure field teams capture and escalate adverse event reports within required timelines
common_challenges: Multi-jurisdiction rules — different countries have different consent, sample, and transparency requirements
Audit readiness — must produce complete audit trails for any field interaction on demand
Real-time enforcement — prefer proactive blocking of non-compliant actions over after-the-fact correction
Content lifecycle — balancing speed of content deployment against compliance review cycle time
Data sovereignty — ensuring personal data stays in the correct geographic region per local regulation

description: First-line sales manager responsible for coaching, developing, and evaluating field representatives. Conducts ride-alongs, reviews call quality, and manages performance.
key_workflows: Coaching visits — accompany reps on field calls, observe interactions, and provide structured feedback
Performance evaluation — score reps against competency frameworks using configurable assessment forms
Goal setting — set and track individual development goals, link coaching outcomes to performance metrics
Team dashboards — monitor team-level metrics (call volume, reach, content utilization, sample compliance)
Coaching reports — generate coaching summaries for HR and leadership review
common_challenges: Form flexibility — coaching assessment forms vary by business unit, country, and therapeutic area
Offline coaching — ride-alongs often occur in low-connectivity clinical environments
Rep buy-in — coaching tools must be fast and non-intrusive during live customer interactions
Objective linking — connecting coaching observations to specific KPI improvements is complex
Data privacy — coaching evaluations contain sensitive personnel data subject to local labor laws

description: Health economics and outcomes research specialist focused on formulary access, pricing, and value demonstration to payers and institutional decision makers.
key_workflows: Payer engagement — track formulary status and reimbursement decisions across health plans and hospital systems
Value dossier distribution — deliver health economics data and outcomes evidence to payer audiences
Access tracking — monitor product access status (formulary tier, step therapy, prior auth requirements) by account
Contract management — support pricing and rebate negotiations with institutional purchasers
Evidence generation — coordinate real-world evidence studies and outcomes data collection
common_challenges: Data fragmentation — payer data, formulary status, and contract terms live in separate systems
Long decision cycles — formulary reviews happen annually; need persistent tracking across quarters
Regulatory boundaries — market access teams operate under different compliance rules than commercial reps
Evidence gap analysis — identifying which outcomes data is needed to win formulary access
Cross-functional alignment — bridging medical, commercial, and market access perspectives for a unified account strategy

description: Technical administrator responsible for platform configuration, integration, data migration, and ongoing system maintenance. The primary technical owner of the CRM platform.
key_workflows: Platform configuration — set up objects, fields, validation rules, permission sets, and custom metadata
Integration management — maintain connections to external systems (master data, ERP, content vault, transparency reporting)
Data migration — plan and execute data loads for HCP/HCO, products, territories, and historical interactions
Release management — test new releases in sandbox, manage feature activation, and coordinate deployments
Monitoring and support — troubleshoot sync errors, manage mobile device enrollment, resolve escalated issues
common_challenges: Packaging complexity — managed package dependencies, namespace conflicts, and upgrade sequencing
Mobile management — supporting multiple device types (iPad, iPhone, Android) with varying OS versions
Sync reliability — ensuring mobile data synchronization is fast, reliable, and conflict-free
Integration brittleness — external system API changes can break data flows without warning
Sandbox management — maintaining representative test environments that mirror production data volumes
